answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a time-vested stake in a shared vault before it earns reputation: clones cost real capital, so a gale of fake identities cannot flood the network for free. Honest agents grow a juniper-like reputation slowly, rooted over many epochs, while detected clones lose their stake to a slashing pool that compensates victims. Identity becomes expensive to fake and cheap to keep honest.
